title: docs(pm-dispatch): an implementation card carries no ADR or skills edits; ADR bookkeeping is filed after the merge
body:
Fixes #32179

domain:skills#3 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CaqHXh17Qc3C7MRAQw

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — internal rules text under `.claude/**`; nothing a metadata author or a customer agent is taught changes

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:派发规则加两行、分诊规则加一行。写代码的卡不再夹带 ADR 或技能文本改动,这类条目各自成为 `domain:skills` 卡;ADR 记账行由落地席在代码合并后立卡并引合并 commit;分诊的 carry note 指向「合并后立卡」。
- 为什么改:裁决记录 6797014134 选 B(原话「32066 C 其他同意」,起因「那skills和adr 就应该单独分拆issue才合理啊」)。此前一行 ADR 记账会把整张代码卡锁到最高模型档,并让代码 PR 等您逐个批准。
- 风险与回滚:纯规则文本,三个文件各自净零行,不新增门禁,不碰冻结的 `dispatch-gates.mjs`。为守行数棘轮删了三行规则,每行在别处仍有家(见 Acceptance notes)。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看:① `references/execution-duties.md` 派发节新增的两行;② 同文件被删的两行与 `references/triage-duties.md` 被删的一行(删得对不对);③ `references/triage-duties.md` 新增的 carry note 行。
- 两分钟验证:跑 `pnpm check:pm-skill-ratchet`,预期 `execution-duties.md is 188 lines (ceiling 188; headroom 0)`、`triage-duties.md is 101 lines (ceiling 101; headroom 0)`,退出码 0。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地(路径面全在 `.claude/**`,档位由席位落地时用 `check-governed-merges` 判定)。

## What changes

Ruling record 6797014134 (letter B), verbatim: "An implementation card's file surface excludes `docs/adr/**`, `skills/**`, `SKILL.md` and `os-dev.md`." / "Those items become their own `domain:skills` cards. The ADR bookkeeping line ("resolved by" or an amended note) is filed by the landing seat after the code merges, citing the merge commit." / "Triage's carry notes point to "file after merge"." / "the landing seat records the owed line at ACCEPT as an Acceptance note with `carrier:`, and files it in the same round."

Text only, three files under `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/`, +5 −5:

| File | Added | Deleted | Lines before → after |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `execution-duties.md` | 2 rules in the dispatch section (the file-surface exclusion; the ADR bookkeeping duty of the landing seat) | 2 rules with a home elsewhere; 1 line re-anchored in place | 188 → 188 |
| `triage-duties.md` | 1 rule (carry notes aimed at those four paths) | 1 rule with a home elsewhere | 101 → 101 |
| `compile-surfaces.md` | — | — (one pointer corrected in place) | 24 → 24 |

Every added bullet is at most 120 bytes (116, 120, 119, and 107 for the re-anchored line). No ceiling row moves; no script changes.

## Tests

No executable behaviour changes, so there is no test to add and no ablation. The readings are the gates below, all taken on head `c702c7d6`.

## Acceptance notes

**Deleted lines and where each rule still lives** (a deleted line that has no other home would be a lost rule):

1. `execution-duties.md`, the line saying standard non-negotiable clauses are not copied into the dispatch prompt. Homes: `.claude/agents/os-dev.md`, the section whose heading says standard clauses live there and not in the prompt, with its first bullet (the prompt carries only the per-card increment); `dispatch-runbook.md`, the bullet that conditional standard clauses are copied only when their criterion is hit; and the same file's own bullet that the prompt carries only the increment. The following line began with "do not cut", which leaned on the deleted line, so it is re-anchored in place to say the card-class constraints always ride the prompt. Same rule, same list.
2. `execution-duties.md`, the line on refusal cases (`code` + `status` minimum) and filter or predicate semantics (compile-surface list declared per surface). Homes: `dispatch-runbook.md`, the three consecutive bullets with the same two triggers and the fuller text (envelope assertion is an os-dev standard clause; the compile-surface list is copied per surface and every surface owes a conclusion in the PR body); `os-dev.md`, the refusal-case envelope clause; `review-checklist.md`, the two bullets checking `code` and `status`.
3. `triage-duties.md`, the "flip-back" line (during implementation the contract turns out to need to move: dev stops, card returns to the decision box, never a silent re-ruling). Homes: `os-dev.md`, the when-to-stop section (a contract-shape change is reported as `needs_decision`; a ruling is never flipped by the dev); `SKILL.md`, the escalation section (the no-escalation classes report a fork the moment product behaviour or contract shape is touched; a dev's `needs_decision` always goes to the human) and its red line that no seat rules on the maintainer's behalf.

**Consequence edit.** `compile-surfaces.md` line 3 pointed at the clause deleted in item 2; it now points at `dispatch-runbook.md`, which holds that clause. One line, in place.

**The grep the order asked for** — every place under `.claude/**` that speaks about ADR or skills edits riding an implementation card, with the action taken:

| Place | What it says | Action |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `references/execution-duties.md`, dispatch section | had no rule | the two rules added here |
| `references/triage-duties.md` | had no carry-note rule | the rule added here |
| `references/lanes/skills.md`, scope section (three bullets) | published skills go through a sub-card filed by triage at first touch; a product-lane PR never edits `skills/**`; internal rules never ride a product PR | none — already agrees with the ruling for `skills/**`; where triage files that sub-card there is no carry note, so the new triage line does not collide with it |
| `SKILL.md`, claim template, the `Skills-docs:` arm | `updated here` covers `skills/**` only on `domain:skills` PRs, else `follow-up #N` | none — this is the line the ruling keeps |
| `SKILL.md`, path-fork section | a mixed diff is not judged by proportion; to split, the dev opens a separate PR | none — still true as the backstop at ACCEPT; the ruling moves the split earlier, it does not remove the backstop |
| `references/review-checklist.md`, scope section | the `Skills-docs:` line is present and true; `follow-up owed` is filed and rewritten to a card number | none — agrees |
| `references/filing-gate.md` | a follow-up owed by landed work is filed as a card; "ride the next PR that touches X" is no carrier | none — this is the rule the ruling's mitigation stands on |
| `references/state-machine.md` | generator output under `skills/**` is judged by `check-governed-merges --test`, never by path | none — generated artifacts are not a card's authored file surface; the carve-out keeps its home here |
| `references/lanes/director.md` | a superseded ADR entry gets a dated note | none — names no implementation card |
| `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` | the `Skills-docs:` line; the two readings owed by a diff touching `skills/**`; the same-PR rule for spec prose | none — no line reads false: the `skills/**` readings now apply to `domain:skills` cards only, and the same-PR rule is about spec prose, not ADRs |
| `.claude/skills/spec-property-retirement/SKILL.md`, the published-skills checklist item | lists the published `SKILL.md` files that teach a retired key among the retirement surfaces, gated by `check:skill-examples` and `check:skill-refs` | not touched — see the first note below |

**Noted, not fixed here (outside this card's file surface):**

- `carrier: the domain:skills seat`. `AGENTS.md`, Context Routing, the `packages/services/**` row: "the PR that creates the package follows the precedent and amends that ADR's status line in the same change". That sentence puts a `docs/adr/**` edit on an implementation PR, which the ruling now excludes. `AGENTS.md` is fenced off in this order, so it stands as written.
- `carrier: the domain:skills seat`. The retirement playbook item above predates this ruling and already sat beside the skills lane's "a product-lane PR never edits `skills/**`". A key removal reds `check:skill-examples` in its own PR while a published skill still teaches the key, so the order of the two cards matters there. That is a sequencing question for the seat, not a one-line fix, and this PR does not make the line read differently than it did.
- The card and the ruling comment call this PR Tier H; the path face is three files, all under `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/`. The tier is the seat's reading at landing.

**Deviations from the dispatch order, each because `os-dev.md` says it wins a conflict:** the body opens with the closing line and carries the declarations before the 速读 block (order: attribution block, signature, 速读, then the closing line); no HTML comment is written, so the seat signature is the plain line under the closing line and there is no `signed:` trailer; the PR carries the claim's `Account:` as assignee (order: no assignee). The two-line session-context attribution block is absent because this subagent's context holds none, and one is not invented.

## Verification
